New in Sentinel 1.21.0 Argus

Names in other alphabets, fewer false alarms, and look-alike wallet addresses.

Every change in this version

Look-alike names

  • A site name written with letters from another alphabet to look like a brand (a PayPal with a Cyrillic letter) is now caught and the card names the brand it copies.
  • Honest international names written in one alphabet, such as münchen.de, no longer get a warning just for being international.
  • The website, the Windows app and the companion read these names the same way.

Fewer false alarms

  • Popular real sites are no longer called misspellings of a brand: elle.com is not Zelle, lacoste.com is not La Poste. A digit or a doubled letter standing in for a brand's letter still alarms.
  • Real words in Spanish, German, French, Portuguese, Italian and Dutch are no longer read as misspelled brands.
  • A name spelled near a brand but made of ordinary words loses its small note when the site is well known or the name has been registered for two years or more.
  • More brands' own sites on other endings are recognised as theirs.

Better detection

  • A link that shows one site and opens another is now noticed when you point at it on a web page, in the Windows app and the companion, not only in email. Email no longer flags ordinary tracking links for this.
  • A copy of a popular site spelled one letter off counts when the name is new or on a throwaway ending.
  • A newly registered name spelled near a brand that asks for a password or a code is treated as a look-alike.

Wallet guard

  • Warns when an address you copy looks like one you copied before but is a different address, a trick called address poisoning. Compare the middle before you send. Your clipboard is never changed.
  • It keeps only the kind of address, its first and last four characters and a scrambled code, for 30 days. Forget copied addresses in Settings clears it.

Fixes

  • Marks beside search results never push a result's title onto a second line.
  • Threat-list updates use less processor time and run at a lower priority.
  • The caution title on light pages is easier to read.
